supersedes: does not replace PREREGISTRATION.json (first pass) -- this is a SECOND, additive pre-registration for the fix pass, per the prompt's instruction
ordering_attestation: Written before any company was re-tested under the new rules and before any return was looked at. The justifications below (A1, A2) cite ONLY coverage/reporting-cadence mechanics -- never a company's outcome or return, and never a reference to which companies would be restored as a result of the rule change.

A1_gap_rule_days.rule: Replace the first pass's '2 consecutive quarters' gap test with a fixed 240-calendar-day threshold between consecutive earnings calls within the coverage window, for every stratum except S4 (S4 uses A2 instead).
A1_gap_rule_days.justification_coverage_only: Ordinary quarterly reporting cadence is approximately 91 days. A single skipped quarter (e.g. a fiscal-calendar irregularity, a switched reporting date, or a one-quarter combined release) produces a gap of roughly 182 days. The first pass's rule measured gaps in QUARTERS (gap_days / 91) and applied a hard 2.0-quarter cutoff, which is equivalent to 182 days -- leaving ZERO headroom past a single skipped quarter before the rule treats the company as having a coverage hole. That is a rounding/measurement-granularity defect, not a substantive coverage requirement: a company with one irregular gap year over an otherwise complete six-year window is not meaningfully less available than one without. 240 days gives headroom of about 58 days beyond a single-skip gap (182 days) without accepting a genuine two-quarter-skip gap (about 273 days), so it preserves the substantive intent of the original rule (catch real coverage holes) while removing the artifact of measuring in imprecise quarter-units.
A1_gap_rule_days.will_be_reported_regardless_of_effect: The full distribution of max-gap-in-days across every candidate, and how many candidates fall within 20 days of the 240-day line on either side, is reported in Step B as a brittleness finding -- not used to retune the threshold.

A2_s4_rule.rule: S4 (failures/distress stratum) uses its own availability rule, separate from A1: (a) at least 4 calls within the coverage window; (b) NO trailing-gap test after the last available call -- the stratum's defining feature is that the company stops reporting because it fails, so a trailing gap is the outcome being studied, not a coverage defect; (c) at least 2 of those calls fall within the 12 months preceding the terminal event (bankruptcy filing, receivership, forced/distressed merger, or delisting); (d) any INTERNAL gap between calls BEFORE the terminal event is still subject to A1's 240-day threshold -- a company that stopped reporting mid-window for reasons unrelated to its eventual failure would still need to show ordinary coverage up to that point.
A2_s4_rule.justification_coverage_only: The first pass's single mechanical rule (12+ calls in the full window, no gap > 2 quarters) structurally cannot be satisfied by a company whose failure ends its reporting history early -- the rule and the stratum's defining event (failure) are in direct tension by construction, independent of any observed outcome or return. A rule for a stratum defined by 'this company failed' cannot simultaneously require 'and it kept behaving like a company that didn't fail for six years.' The fix separates 'was this company covered while it was still an active reporter' (part a/c/d, testable) from 'did it keep reporting after failing' (which by definition it did not, and dropping it for that is circular).

A4_s4_weighting_disclosure.statement: S4 is defined by outcome (companies known in advance to have failed or nearly failed) and therefore over-represents distress relative to any real, ex-ante population of companies in this universe. Every ruler figure downstream of this corpus (outcome balance, detection-threshold projection, cost estimate) MUST be reported BOTH including and excluding S4, with S4's share of total companies and total calls stated explicitly each time it appears.

A5_ticker_alias_resolution.ordering_attestation: Written before any alias candidate was queried against the vendor and before any return was looked at. The reasoning below cites ONLY vendor symbol-list/coverage mechanics -- never a company's outcome or return, and never a reference to which companies would be restored as a result of alias resolution.
A5_ticker_alias_resolution.rule: For every company currently failing availability because the vendor returned zero or near-zero events, test whether the failure is an IDENTITY problem (the company's data exists in the vendor under a different symbol) rather than a genuine coverage gap, before accepting the zero-event reading as final. Identity resolution changes NO eligibility rule and NO availability threshold: a company recovered under an alias must still pass exactly the same stratum rule (A1's 240-day rule, or A2's S4 failures-stratum rule) it faced under its original symbol. This is bookkeeping -- correcting which vendor row corresponds to which company -- not a relaxation of any registered rule.
A5_ticker_alias_resolution.justification_coverage_only: A vendor's symbol table is a flat list keyed on a single ticker string; it has no concept of share classes, renames, or post-bankruptcy delisted symbols. Two structural reasons a vendor can show zero events for a real, well-covered company: (1) dual-class equity, where the vendor may key transcripts to one class's ticker (e.g. GOOG) while the company is tracked here under the other (GOOGL) -- both tickers denote calls given by the same company, so this is a lookup-key mismatch, not missing coverage; (2) a company that underwent bankruptcy or receivership typically continues trading briefly under a modified/delisted symbol (commonly the original ticker plus a 'Q' suffix, or a five-letter OTC form) -- the vendor may carry that post-event symbol as a distinct row from the original, pre-event ticker this corpus queried. Testing both is a coverage-mechanics check, not an outcome-driven one: the candidate aliases are generated from public share-class and delisting-symbol conventions, not from knowledge of what either company's earnings-call content would say.
A5_ticker_alias_resolution.scope: Applies only to companies whose current availability failure is a ZERO or near-zero vendor event count (not a genuine measured gap under A1/A2). On the evidence in CORPUS_MANIFEST_V2.json as of this addendum: GOOGL (S5) and SIVB (S4) show exactly 0 events. HON and UPS (S1) also show 0/null events and in_vendor_symbol_list=False in the manifest, carried forward from the first pass without having been re-queried in the fix pass -- these are added to this run's candidate list for the same identity check, since the same lookup-key-mismatch mechanism could equally apply, even though neither HON nor UPS has a known share-class or bankruptcy history; a plain vendor symbol-list lookup will settle whether that is a query artifact or genuine absence. This is a widening of the candidate list to what the manifest evidence actually shows, not a change to the rule in the paragraph above.
A5_ticker_alias_resolution.will_be_reported_regardless_of_effect: Every alias candidate tried and its raw vendor result is reported in the wrap-up, including if resolution recovers nothing -- which would itself be a finding confirming the original zero-event reading was a genuine coverage gap, not an identity artifact.

A6_terminal_value_grading.ordering_attestation: This is GRADING a known outcome, not SELECTING which companies to include. All five S4 companies (WOLF, NOVA, FRC, RMO, SUNW) were frozen into the corpus in the prior run's fix Step C, before any return was measured for any of them -- see CORPUS_MANIFEST_V2.json's step_e_split and the fix-pass notes in analysis/data/run_state/corpus-construction/progress.json. Deciding how to score a return that could not previously be computed (because the price series has no data past a delisting event) is a downstream grading-rule question, not a membership decision, and does not reopen or re-run any eligibility test.
A6_terminal_value_grading.rule: Use actual cached prices wherever they exist (analysis/data/corpus_v2/corpus_v2_price_cache.json). Where a company's 182-day forward window from its last call extends past its last trading day, use the company's TERMINAL VALUE for the end-of-window price instead of a missing real price. Where equity was verified wiped out (zero recovery to common shareholders), terminal value is ZERO, so forward return is exactly -100% (this holds for ANY positive entry price, so no new entry-price fetch is needed to apply the rule) and the outcome grades as 'lags the benchmark' under the existing +/-5 point dead band.
A6_terminal_value_grading.guard_against_over_application: Terminal value is zero ONLY where equity was verified wiped out. A company acquired for cash or stock has a POSITIVE terminal value (the deal consideration), not zero. Checked whether any other corpus company was acquired during the 2020-2025 window before applying zero to any name -- see the wrap-up for the check performed and its result.
A6_terminal_value_grading.rmo_note: RMO removed from the corpus entirely per Luis's explicit instruction (Step D of this same prompt) -- not graded under A6, not a candidate for it.
A6_terminal_value_grading.verification_sources_summary: Full citations recorded per-company in analysis/corpus_construction_outcomes_v3_terminal.py's TERMINAL_OVERRIDES and restated in the wrap-up. Sunnova (NOVA): Chapter 11 filed 2025-06-08 (SEC 8-K), NYSE delisting 2025-06-23, confirmed plan with zero equity recovery effective 2025-11-14. Sunworks (SUNW): Chapter 7 liquidation petition filed 2024-02-05 (SEC 8-K), Nasdaq delisting notice 2024-02-06; ticker continued trading OTC as SUNWQ at near-zero prices post-delisting -- graded as terminal zero because the residual value is immaterial against the +/-5pp dead band, stated not hidden. First Republic (FRC): FDIC receivership 2023-05-01 (FDIC.gov failed-bank record), assets/deposits acquired by JPMorgan Chase, common equity holders received no recovery per standard FDIC receivership priority.
A6_terminal_value_grading.finding_not_anticipated_by_the_prompt: The prompt's framing ('their price series end when they fail') implies partial pre-failure price data exists in the cache. It does not: analysis/data/corpus_v2/corpus_v2_price_cache.json holds a fully EMPTY {} for all four of NOVA, SUNW, FRC, RMO -- no price data at any date, not just post-failure. This did not block grading only because terminal value zero makes the forward return exactly -100% independent of the (unfetched, and under this run's constraints unfetchable) entry price.

A8_price_coverage_gate.ordering_attestation: Registered before examining any company's price coverage or return. This is a COVERAGE rule -- it tests whether a company CAN be graded, not what its outcome IS. No company's return, direction, or 2020-2025 outcome was looked at before this addendum was written; the two motivating cases (Sunnova, Wolfspeed) were already publicly documented failures of the price PROVIDER (purged history / restructuring), not selections made because of an outcome.
A8_price_coverage_gate.justification_scope_restriction: This addendum's justification rests ONLY on: (a) Sunnova's price provider (Yahoo/yfinance) returning zero rows for its entire 2020-2025 window, not just post-delisting -- see wrap-ups/corpus-fix-5-expand-and-prices-out.md; (b) Wolfspeed's price history under its current ticker starting only 2025-09-29 post-Chapter-11 restructuring, leaving 23 of 28 corpus calls with no price at all -- same wrap-up. NO justification here references any company's return, direction, or which companies would pass or fail this gate -- that is determined in Step B, after this rule is fixed.
A8_price_coverage_gate.rule: A call is gradable when EITHER (1) real prices exist for the company AND for SPY on the call date and at the close of its 182-day forward window, OR (2) the terminal-value rule (A6) applies -- the company's equity was verified wiped out and the window closes after that event. A company PASSES this gate when it has at least 12 gradable calls under this definition.
A8_price_coverage_gate.threshold_reasoning: 12 matches A1's existing 12-call minimum for ordinary availability, so the two rules agree on what counts as a usable company rather than applying a second, independently-chosen number. Inherited, not independently derived for price coverage specifically -- stated as a limitation in the wrap-up.
identity_resolution_order_before_failing: 3. post-event forms -- the 'Q' suffix, five-letter delisted variants, and a documented pre-merger predecessor ticker (e.g. Wolfspeed traded as CREE before its 2021 rename)
A8_price_coverage_gate.identity_resolution_note: A company is not failed for an identity problem. Every symbol tried and what it returned is recorded per-company in COVERAGE_GATE_SWEEP.json; any newly-working symbol is added to TICKER_ALIASES.json.
